answer: Each agent’s voting weight can be tied to a unique, nontransferable deposit locked for a fixed period, with rewards released only after the agent completes verifiable work. Creating a hundred fake identities then requires a hundred deposits; splitting one deposit among them does not multiply weight. A public cipher can bind each claim to its deposit, while a ledge in the workflow delays withdrawal until checks finish. The attacker pays in scarce capital and time, and risks losing the deposit for proven fraud; timber is only an analogy for the real resource being consumed.
